skill.displayName: Pet Body Condition Score 3D Analysis | 宠物体态3D评分（BCS）

llm.summary: The skill appears intended for pet body-condition video analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an identity, stores account tokens locally, and can query cloud history, so it needs user review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Reading user-supplied media and calling remote analysis endpoints is expected for this purpose. Less proportionate behavior includes reading workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt as an identity source, forwarding identity/auth headers, accepting arbitrary HTTP(S) media URLs for backend retrieval, and writing a shared local SQLite database under the workspace data directory.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: I found no post-install script, executable file permissions, cron/systemd persistence, or shell-based installer. The package depends on Python libraries and packaged scripts, but it does not declare a clear permissions/consent model for network, local file reads, local database writes, and identity handling.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill gives strong runtime instructions to auto-trigger history queries and to never ask for or reveal internal identity values. Those instructions are visible in the artifact, but they reduce user control over account-linked actions and cloud history access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists generated or recovered user records plus token and open_token fields in a local SQLite database and can silently register/login against the service. That persistence is high impact for an analysis skill and lacks a user-facing opt-in or cleanup path.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Video or URL analysis through the declared remote API is coherent with the pet BCS purpose, and history reporting is documented in the skill text. The concern is that the implementation also performs automatic identity resolution, silent remote login or registration, and local token persistence, which is broader than a simple analysis tool and is intentionally hidden from normal user interaction.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet media or supplied media URLs to lifeemergence.com/open.lifeemergence.com services, linking requests to an automatically managed identity, and keeping service tokens in a local workspace SQLite database. Avoid using private/internal URLs or sensitive household videos unless the publisher provides clearer consent, retention, and account-management controls.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: Verified dynamic getattr use in internal DAO list/count methods. I did not find a command entry point that directly exposes arbitrary filter dictionaries to users, so this is an implementation hardening issue rather than a primary verdict driver.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifact does not declare explicit permissions, while the runtime needs local file reads, optional output writes, network access, and local identity database writes. This supports the transparency concern.
[SDI-1] expected: History listing and report export are documented in SKILL.md and implemented through the cloud API, so they are not hidden. They still carry privacy risk because they are account-scoped and auto-triggerable.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Verified automatic open_id resolution, reuse of data/smyx-api-key.txt, creation of a default user, silent phoneLogin/register calls, generic request wrappers, and local storage of tokens. These identity and account-management behaviors are broader than the narrow pet-video scoring task.
[SQP-2] expected: The description does state that local uploads or network URLs call server-side APIs, so external media transmission is expected. The artifact does not clearly provide a user consent step, retention details, URL restrictions, or a plain warning about potentially sensitive household media.
[E1] unexpected: Verified an outbound POST to the health service phoneLogin endpoint with silent registration fields. That is not necessary to understand as pet BCS analysis and is a material account-linkage concern.
[P2] expected: The reported invisible character appears to be a zero-width joiner used in emoji formatting in visible table rows, not hidden evaluator instructions. Markdown report-link rendering is expected, but API-returned links should still be treated as untrusted output.
[YR4] expected: The manifest is highly prescriptive, but I did not find artifact-backed deception or hidden override text. The metadata-poisoning signal is downgraded; the verdict is driven by identity, account, and persistence behavior instead.
